note: Authored join-code format data (issue #1111). This file is the ONE place
the join-identifier scheme is written down: gui/join-code.js reads it in
the browser (fetch), tests/client/join-code.test.js reads it from disk,
and worker-rendezvous/src/registry.js imports it into the rendezvous
service bundle. Nothing else may hardcode an alphabet, a GUID or a
denied word.
JSON rather than TOML because those three consumers must all read it with
no parser dependency and no build step: the browser client ships as plain
ES modules and a Cloudflare Worker bundles with esbuild. Neither can parse
TOML. The per-entry 'reason' fields carry what comments would.
Design source: docs/gdd/systems/native-network-foundation.md 'Join-code
model' and pasm/spec/design/p2p-design-deltas.yaml decision
p2p-human-readable-join-namespaces.
Five typed letters. The alphabet deliberately EXCLUDES L, because L
normalises to I — a letter that can never survive canonicalisation must
never be minted, or the printed code would not round-trip through the
very normalisation that makes it typeable. O and I stay in: they are the
canonical forms of 0 and 1. J stays distinct and is minted normally.
Two stable project GUIDs, one per join type, so a suffix typed into the
crew field can never silently resolve a fleet host. These values are
permanent — changing one orphans every printed code of that type.
'client' is what a phone/console types; 'server' admits ship hosts to a
fleet (issue #1114 owns joining it; #1111 only needs it to EXIST so a
wrong-type answer is distinguishable from an unknown one).
One version GUID marks a compatible release. Bump it when a release can
no longer join a host built from the previous one, so the rendezvous can
answer 'version-mismatch' instead of 'unknown' for a suffix that is
registered under an older build. This is ADVISORY discovery help only:
the authoritative protocol/content check is the host's own delivery
stamp handshake (src/delivery/stamp.rs, delivery::check_join_stamp).
